headline: IBM develops 0.7nm-class technology with 50% higher performance
summary: IBM's new 0.7nm-class tech offers up to 50% higher performance and 70% higher energy efficiency
details: IBM has produced a test chip using its 0.7nm-class fabrication technology, the industry's first sub-1nm manufacturing process. This new tech uses two wafers and ultra-thin dielectric bonding.
The 0.7nm-class process offers up to 50% higher performance and 70% higher energy efficiency compared to IBM's 2nm-class node. It also provides a 40% higher SRAM density.

IBM's nanostack transistor architecture uses two wafers for active transistor tiers, allowing for independent optimization of n-type and p-type transistors. This approach enables significant improvements in power, performance, and area.

headline: Practical Guide: Building Structured Inter-Agent Communication
summary: A new guide on DEV for reliable multi-agent systems
details: The article 'Building Structured Inter-Agent Communication: A Practical Guide' on DEV provides a practical approach to creating reliable multi-agent systems. It focuses on the importance of structured communication between agents.

The guide emphasizes the use of typed contracts and schema validation to ensure deterministic behavior in agent pipelines. This approach helps prevent errors and ensures that agents interact reliably.
By following this guide, developers can create more robust and testable multi-agent systems. The article is available on the DEV platform.
